title: On Stochastic Continuous-Time Linear System Identification for Adaptive Stabilization
abstract: arXiv:2611.02340v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: System identification studies the canonical problem of reliably learning system-dynamics from state and input trajectories. One of its important applications consists of estimating a feedback gain matrix that can stabilize an unknown system. This paper focuses on the analysis of such adaptive stabilization schemes for multivariate linear time-invariant state-space models. The system instability practically renders trajectories short, i.e., the observed data is notably limited. So, it is crucial to tightly consider effects of \emph{all} involved quantities including length and number of trajectories, dimension, controllability Gramian, and signal-to-noise ratio. We put forward a simple, practical, and reliable relationship between the chance that adaptive stabilization (based on system identification) fails to stabilize the system, in terms of all the above-mentioned quantities. translated_title: 关于用于自适应镇定的随机连续时间线性系统辨识
translated_abstract: 系统辨识研究的是从状态和输入轨迹中可靠地学习系统动态这一经典问题。其重要应用之一是估计能够镇定未知系统的反馈增益矩阵。本文聚焦于对多变量线性时不变状态空间模型的自适应镇定方案的分析。系统的不稳定性实际上使得轨迹较短，即观测到的数据相当有限。因此，紧密考虑所有相关量的影响至关重要，包括轨迹的长度和数量、维度、可控性Gramian矩阵以及信噪比。我们提出了一个简单、实用且可靠的关系，用以刻画基于系统辨识的自适应镇定未能镇定系统的概率与上述所有量之间的联系。我们的发现表明，尽管存在指数级的影响……
tldr: 本文提出了基于系统辨识的自适应镇定的失败概率与轨迹长度和数量、维度、可控性Gramian矩阵及信噪比等所有相关量之间简单、实用且可靠的定量关系。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes a simple, practical, and reliable relationship between the failure probability of identification-based adaptive stabilization and all relevant quantities, including trajectory length and number, dimension, controllability Gramian, and signal-to-noise ratio.
